x: Reigate relay: Jon Blackledge – The kid leads the day to hand selectors a headache. AAA 4-stage: Phil Wicks – Straight back on his horse after Sutton stitch.
Jon Blackledge handled the conditions well and stayed with the breakaway group of three but blistered in the last two laps to fall back and take third in the A.

Then to the 1500 which included our surprise – Neil Speaight – who has been busy on the International circuit for the last few years and was making a welcome return to our team backed by Jon Blackledge who had run a pb in Belgium a few days earlier.
Now, what could Jon Blackledge do, the first of three short-stagers that would hopefully hammer in some spikes to help us climb into the medals?

On the track Jon Blackledge moved down in distance to gain third spot in the A 800. Joe van de Toorn found himself in what was to be a faster race in the B 800m going through in 53 sec and predictably suffering from 200m out.
In the B event Jon Blackledge had to take the lead on lap one as the swirling wind prevented any breakaways. Even then the bell was reached in only 58 secs.

A pretty safe bet for a winning Belgrave relay team were elsewhere – “Jonesy” and “Polly” training at altitude in Morocco, “Sp8y” in the USA, Jim Kelly also over the water for a family wedding, Steve Davies taking a break, and then, two days before the race, Jon Blackledge pulling out with a calf problem.
